title: Autoscaling-aware geo-hint steering with circuit-breaker safeguards
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During recent peak events we've seen an interplay between autoscaling delays in Dedicated pools and aggressive geo-fallback logic that routes traffic to remote regions, causing elevated tail latency and unexpected cost spikes. We need a routing policy that: 1) prefers local/geo-pinned pools, 2) avoids routing into regions that are transiently underprovisioned because autoscaling has not caught up, and 3) inserts circuit-breaker style safeguards to prevent cascading failovers and wide-area shedding.

Goal: Design and implement an autoscaling-aware steering policy that consumes capacity and scaling signals from regional schedulers, biases by latency and geo-pinning preferences, and applies per-region circuit-breakers and incremental shedding thresholds to maintain SLOs and cost targets. The policy should be pluggable into the request director and observable from Console dashboards.

Scope: Server-side routing logic and config surfaces (API + Console). Does NOT include changes to autoscaler implementation beyond exposing existing metrics/signals. Initial rollout targets hosted + Dedicated pools in NA/EU (us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1).

Out of scope: client-side SDK changes, network-level geo-DNS changes, VPC-only private control plane changes (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy reads region capacity_hint and scaling_state signals and prefers regions with predicted capacity >= request cost
When a region reports scaling_state=SCALING_UP or predicted_shortfall > threshold, director reduces weight and applies gradual shed percentage instead of full failover
Per-region circuit-breaker trips if 5xx rate > 3% and p99 latency > 3x SLO over a 1m window, and remains open for exponential backoff windows
Dashboard surfaces per-region routing weights, open circuit-breakers, and predicted_shortfall metric; alert when shed > 5% cluster-wide
Feature toggles allow: full enable, monitoring-only, and canary by customer tag for Dedicated customers
design_notes: Architecture: introduce a SteeringDecision stage in request director that evaluates: locality_score (geo pinning + latency hint), capacity_risk_score (predicted_shortfall / outstanding_scaled_capacity), and stability_score (recent error + latency trends). Final weight = softmax(locality_score - alpha*capacity_risk_score + beta*stability_score) with configurable alpha/beta per deployment tier.

Autoscaling signals: use scheduler-exposed metrics: predicted_shortfall (tokens/req per minute), scaling_state {STABLE, SCALING_UP, SCALING_DOWN}, and target_utilization. Do NOT rely on instantaneous queue depth alone.

Circuit-breaker: hybrid quota + statistical breaker. Quota allows limited emergency traffic into a degraded region; statistical breaker watches p99 and error-rate and flips to open on breach. When open, region gets 0 weight except for emergency quota flow. Exponential backoff uses base 10s, max 10m.

Load-shedding: apply prioritized shedding at director using request_cost buckets (small/normal/large). Large requests are shed earlier during capacity-risk conditions. This preserves latency for small interactive calls (chat) while protecting throughput for embeddings/large-batch workloads.

Tradeoffs: stronger capacity bias reduces failovers but may increase local latency if local region degrades. Config defaults favor SLO preservation for P1 customers and cost preservation for low-tier customers via flags.
Backward compatibility: default config set to monitoring-only. We will gate full enablement behind runtime flag and per-customer policy in CustomerConfig service.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (monitoring-only, 1 week): Collect capacity_hint and scaling_state in director metrics; validate signal integrity against autoscaler metrics (Grafana dashboards).
Phase 1 (canary, 2 weeks): Enable steering decision in canary for internal test customers and 5% traffic for low-risk routes. Observe p99 and error rate vs baseline.
Phase 2 (tiered rollout, 3-4 weeks): Enable for non-critical hosted tenants, then Dedicated test customers who opt-in. Enable circuit-breaker enforcement gradually (monitoring -> dry-run -> enforce).
Phase 3 (full): Flip default to enabled for P1 customers and enable per-customer toggles. Monitor for two production incidents before removing monitoring-only flag.
Rollback plan: emergency toggle to disable steering (director falls back to current latency-based pinning), and global fail-open override to prefer lowest-cost routing for short window.
metrics: SLOs to track: p95 latency, p99 latency, 5xx rate per-region and global
New metrics: region_predicted_shortfall, director_region_weight, director_breaker_state (CLOSED/HALF_OPEN/OPEN), shed_rate_by_request_class
Business metrics: cross-region egress cost delta, unit token cost by region
Alerts: region_predicted_shortfall > 0.10 for 5m; open_breakers >= 2 regions for 2m; shed_rate > 5% cluster-wide
testing_plan: Unit tests for SteeringDecision math (alpha/beta sensitivity ranges).
Integration tests simulating autoscaler signals: inject SCALING_UP/SCALING_DOWN and verify routing weight transitions and shedding percentages.
Chaos test: during canary run, kill a regional pool and confirm circuit-breaker trips and traffic ramps to other healthy regions without saturating them.
Load tests: run mixed workload (chat + embeddings) to validate prioritized shedding preserves small request p95 while protecting throughput.
Runbook verification: exercise rollback toggle in staging and validate dashboards/alerts trigger correctly.
